Uses of Record Class
io.webagent4j.locator.api.LocatorDefinition

Packages that use LocatorDefinition
Package
Description
io.webagent4j.action
Verified browser actions: one explicit, bounded command pipeline per interaction, with three terminal modes - real execution, dryRun(), and plan() - that all share the exact same target-resolution and precondition logic so they can never disagree.
io.webagent4j.browser
Backend-neutral browser, page, and frame contracts - no Playwright (or other native backend) type appears in any public signature here.
io.webagent4j.extraction
 
io.webagent4j.extraction.api
Backend-neutral extraction request/result/provenance contracts, converters, validators, and the extraction-specific failure taxonomy - depends only on webagent4j-locator-api, never on webagent4j-dom.
io.webagent4j.locator
 
io.webagent4j.locator.api
Immutable, backend-neutral locator definitions and the fluent query contracts every semantic search builds on - IFind and ILocator contain no engine logic and no backend-native type.
io.webagent4j.locator.internal
 
io.webagent4j.observation
The immutable semantic observation model, options, renderers, diff, fingerprint, and the batch-capture backend SPI (io.webagent4j.observation.spi) - depends on webagent4j-dom and webagent4j-locator-api only, never on a browser backend.
io.webagent4j.verification
Deterministic, side-effect-free, pollable conditions over current page state - used both as action postconditions (IPreparedAction#expect(...)) and standalone.

  • Uses of LocatorDefinition in io.webagent4j.extraction

    Methods in io.webagent4j.extraction with parameters of type LocatorDefinition
    Modifier and Type
    Method
    Description
    ExtractionResult<ExtractedTable>
    ExtractionEngine.extractTable(ILiveLocatorContext context, LocatorDefinition source)
    Resolves source to one accessible HTML table (ILocatorEngine.locateSingle(io.webagent4j.locator.LocatorContext, io.webagent4j.locator.api.LocatorDefinition)) and reads its structure: headers from the table's own direct thead > tr > th/ thead > tr > td (empty when the table has no thead - never guessed from an untagged first row), and every direct tbody/tfoot/table-level tr not inside a thead, each row's cells read from its own direct th/td children in DOM order.
